svg.title: Numbness and tingling are localized first, central or peripheral: a thalamic lesion gives opposite-side clumsiness and burning pain, a spinal cord lesion a truncal sensory level with brisk reflexes, a root a dermatomal pattern with a lost reflex, a mononeuropathy one nerve's territory, a length-dependent polyneuropathy symmetric distal sensory loss, and Guillain-Barre syndrome weakness ascending over days with lost reflexes; a neuronopathy hits the cell body; each column gives what it looks like, the test that settles it and what to do, then the nerve pathology behind it (functional block, Wallerian degeneration and the three grades of nerve injury after trauma, dying back, demyelination)
